aws-c9gd-v1.description: Single-operation benchmarks with dedicated Konifer and k6 hosts, RDS PostgreSQL, and S3 Standard.
interpretation: Konifer and k6 use separate EC2 instances; both instances and the single-AZ RDS primary must share an availability zone.
Konifer is limited to 4 CPUs and 6 GiB RAM. k6 is limited to 1 CPU and 1536 MiB RAM on c9g.medium.
Scratch is local NVMe instance storage mounted at /app/tmp, not tmpfs or EBS. It is disposable; images and metadata live in S3 and RDS.

k6 uses Konifer's private address. The harness always requests plaintext database connections with ssl-mode disable and RDS force_ssl off, regardless of Konifer version. Older JDBC schedulers may ignore the setting and negotiate TLS using driver defaults. Administrative connections verify TLS. S3 uses HTTPS through a gateway endpoint and S3 Standard is regional, not AZ-local.
This profile is a deployment target, not a completed benchmark. Verify regional instance availability and record the exact AMI, image digest, AZ, and RDS engine version before publishing results.
Compare releases only within this environment. Change the environment ID when instance sizes, limits, scratch storage, or database configuration materially change.

local-compose-v4.description: Compare releases with one operation in flight, fixed sample counts, and Garage object storage.
interpretation: Resource limits: Konifer, 2 CPUs and 8 GiB RAM; PostgreSQL and Garage, 1 CPU and 1 GiB RAM each.
Konifer, PostgreSQL, Garage, and k6 share this laptop's CPU, memory, and storage.
Operation benchmarks use single-vu-v1: warmup and measurement run in sequence, with one operation in flight. Eager uploads wait for background variants outside the acceptance timer.
Compare releases within this environment. The earlier arrival-rate environments use a different measurement protocol. These runs do not measure production capacity.
